title: Employer Direct Early Intervention Under the Workers' Compensation Referral
content:
# Employer direct programs

**Terms.** An employer direct program of the Workers' Compensation Referral (Employer Direct Early Intervention) is opened only from the employer's incident report and under the employer's contract. It covers first-aid-level care only where the program is limited to first aid, never files a claim with a carrier, and is invoiced to the employer every employer invoice cycle in calendar days, with payment due the program's payment-due period in calendar days after the invoice.

**When the direct program ends.** Once the worker has used the program's direct-pay visit cap — counted as all visits recorded on the referral over its life — or needs care beyond first aid, the employer must report the injury to its carrier, and further care is a new Workers' Comp Outpatient Therapy referral.

## Conditions and consequences

| Condition on the employer direct referral | Consequence |
|---|---|
| opened | only from the employer's incident report, under the employer's contract |
| billing | invoiced to the employer on the invoice cycle; never a claim with a carrier |
| visits recorded reach the direct-pay visit cap | employer reports the injury to its carrier; further care is a new Workers' Comp Outpatient Therapy referral |
| the worker needs care beyond first aid | the same consequence as reaching the cap |

## Case (hypothetical, for a direct-pay visit cap of 4)

Four visits have been recorded on a worker's Employer Direct Early Intervention referral. The cap is reached: the employer must report the injury to its carrier, and any further care is given under a new Workers' Comp Outpatient Therapy referral rather than the direct program.
